newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac sees 10-15 pct rise in housing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac sees 10-15 pct rise in housing.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Tuesday it expected to see housing starts to rise by about 10 to 15 percent in 1997 compared to 1996 levels.
"We do see some upturn next year. I think there will be more new home starts next year than this year, perhaps up to 10 to 15 percent," managing director Bob Joss told a news conference.

Joss said Westpac also saw continued moves from home owners to refinance loans. "It's a very competitive market. I would expect there to be continued tightening of home loan margins as there is more securitising and more origination done off a bank's balance sheet, as opposed to on," he said.

Joss later said it would be tough for Westpac to increase absolute profit in the 1996/97 financial year, but that the bank saw earnings per share a little bit higher because of a planned share buyback.
Westpac earlier reported that its net profit before abnormals rose 11.5 percent to A$1.132 billion from A$1.015 billion the previous year.
Westpac shares closed 15 cents weaker at A$7.05.
